λαγχανω.gloss: I obtain by lot, cast lots
λαγχανω.def: (a) I obtain (receive) by lot, my lot (turn) is, (b) I draw lots.

λαζαροσ.def: Lazarus, Eliezer, (a) the beggar, (b) the brother of Martha and Mary, of Bethany.

λαιλαψ.def: a sudden storm, squall, whirlwind, hurricane.

λαλεω.def: (I talk, chatter in classical Greek, but in NT a more dignified word) I speak, say.

λαλια.def: (in classical Greek: babble, chattering) speech, talk; manner of speech, dialect.

λαμβανω.def: (a) I receive, get, (b) I take, lay hold of.

λαμεχ.def: (Hebrew), Lamech, son of Methuselah and father of Noah.

λανθανω.def: I am hidden (concealed), lie hid, escape notice, sometimes with acc. of person from whom concealment takes place; I do so and so unconsciously, unknown to myself, I shut my eyes to so and so.

λαοδικεια.def: Laodicea, a city in the Lycos valley in the Roman province Asia, near Colossae and Hierapolis.

λαοδικευσ.def: a Laodicean, an inhabitant of Laodicea.

λαοσ.def: (a) a people, characteristically of God's chosen people, first the Jews, then the Christians, (b) sometimes, but rarely, the people, the crowd.

λασαια.def: Lasea, a city in Crete, about the middle of the south coast.

λασκω.gloss: I burst asunder with a loud noise
λασκω.def: I burst asunder with a loud noise.

λατρεια.def: service rendered to God, perhaps simply: worship.

λατρευω.def: I serve, especially God, perhaps simply: I worship.

λεββαιοσ.def: Lebbaeus, a pet-name for Thaddaeus, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus; the full form of the name is not known.

λεγεων.def: properly: a division of the Roman army, numbering about 6,000 infantry with additional cavalry; hence: a very large number; a legion.

λεγω.def: (denoting speech in progress), (a) I say, speak; I mean, mention, tell, (b) I call, name, especially in the pass., (c) I tell, command.

λειπω.gloss: I am wanting, am left behind
λειπω.def: (earlier: I leave behind, abandon), (a) I am wanting, (b) mid: e.g. with gen: I come behind (in a race), am left behind in, fall short of (some standard), am wanting in.

λειτουργεω.def: I act in the public service, render service, minister, in the widest sense, of some special public religious service, but also of the service of priests and Levites.

λειτουργια.def: a charitable gift, public service in the widest sense; service as of priest or Levite ritual.

λειτουργοσ.def: a minister, servant, of an official character; of priests and Levites.

λεπισ.def: a scale, a scaly substance thrown off from the body.

λεπτον.def: a small piece of money, probably the smallest piece of money.

λευι.def: (Hebrew), Levi, (a) an ancestor of Jesus, (b) another ancestor of Jesus, (c) third son of Jacob, the patriarch, and founder of a tribe named after him, (d) son of Alphaeus, and called Matthew, a revenue officer and one of the twelve apostles of Jesus.

λευισ.def: (Hebrew), Levi, son of Alphaeus, the publican.

λευιτησ.def: a Levite, properly a man of the tribe of Levi; hence: a priest's assistant, an under priest, as the members of that tribe were charged with this duty.

λευιτικοσ.def: belonging to the tribe of Levi; Levitical.

λιβερτινοσ.def: a freedman, one of the class of manumitted slaves; a synagogue at Jerusalem appears to have been reserved for them.

λιθοβολεω.def: I stone, cast stones (at), kill by stoning.

λιθοσ.def: a stone; met: of Jesus as the chief stone in a building.

λιθοστρωτον.def: (adj: paved with stone), a mosaic pavement.

λικμαω.def: I crush to powder, scatter like chaff.

λιτρα.def: a Roman pound, of about twelve ounces.

λιψ.def: the south-west wind, and thus the quarter from which it comes.

λογια.def: a collection, collecting (of money), particularly of an irregular local contribution for religious purposes.

λογιζομαι.def: I reckon, count, charge with; reason, decide, conclude; think, suppose.

λογικοσ.def: (a) reasonable, rational, (b) metaphorical, as contrasted with the literal.

λογιον.def: plur: oracles, divine responses or utterances (it can include the entire Old Testament).

λογομαχια.def: contention about words, an unprofitable controversy.

λογοσ.gloss: a word, speech, divine utterance, analogy
λογοσ.def: a word, speech, divine utterance, analogy.

λοιδορεω.def: I revile a person to his face, abuse insultingly.

λοιπον.gloss: finally, from now on, henceforth, beyond that
λοιπον.def: finally, from now on, henceforth, beyond that.

λοιποσ.def: left, left behind, the remainder, the rest, the others.

λουκασ.def: Lucas, Luke, Christian physician and writer of the Third Gospel and Acts.

λουκιοσ.def: Lucius, (a) of Cyrene, an early Christian, in the church of Antioch, by some identified with the evangelist Luke, (b) a Christian with Paul at Corinth, by some identified with (a).

λουτρον.def: a bath (of water, not the vessel), water for washing, washing.

λουω.def: (lit. or merely ceremonially), I wash, bathe (the body); mid: of washing, bathing one's self; met: I cleanse from sin.

λυδδα.def: Lydda, Diospolis, Lod (modern Ludd), a city on the way to Joppa within a day's journey of Jerusalem.

λυδια.def: Lydia, a lady resident of Philippi, native of Thyatira in Lydia (Asia Minor), and engaged in the clothing trade.

λυκαονια.def: Lycaonia, the country of the Lykaones, a district of Asia Minor, comprised within the Roman province Galatia and including the cities of Derbe and Lystra.

λυκια.def: Lycia, a small Roman province on the south coast of Asia Minor.

λυκοσ.def: a wolf, of perhaps a jackal; often applied to persons of wolfish proclivities.

λυσιασ.def: Claudius Lysias, a Roman tribune of the soldiers in Jerusalem.

λυσιτελεω.def: it is advantageous to, it profits.

λυστρα.def: Lystra, a Lycaonian city in the southern part of the Roman province Galatia.

λυτρον.gloss: a ransom, an offering of expiation
λυτρον.def: the purchasing money for manumitting slaves, a ransom, the price of ransoming; especially the sacrifice by which expiation is effected, an offering of expiation.

λυτροω.def: I release on receipt of ransom; mid: I redeem, release by paying ransom, liberate.

λυτρωσισ.def: (in the Old Testament: ransoming from imprisonment for debt, or from slavery, release from national misfortune, etc.), liberation, deliverance, release.

λυω.def: (a) I loose, untie, release, (b) met: I break, destroy, set at naught, contravene; I break up a meeting, annul.
